--- title: "Interface parameters and Kd" subtitle: "Do interface descriptors from predicted structures estimate binding affinity better than PRODIGY?" --- ::: {.backfilled-note} **Every result on this page is backfilled.** The numbers were transcribed from `bench20/RUNLOG.md` and the output CSVs of a run that completed before this site existed, not produced by executing code from this site. The output files are real and are served from the run directories; the surrounding analysis was not re-executed. Each run records `code_version: null`, because the commit that produced it is not identified. ::: ## The question PDBBind gives crystal structures with measured Kd. PRODIGY predicts affinity from a structure and is the baseline to beat. The hypothesis was that a richer set of interface descriptors — buried area, hydrogen bonds, shape complementarity, Rosetta interface energies, PLIP interaction counts — would predict Kd better, and that AlphaFold models could stand in for crystal structures so the method would work on complexes with no solved structure. That is two claims: that predicted structures are good enough, and that interface descriptors beat PRODIGY. The first largely holds. The second does not, at this sample size. ## The benchmark set ::: {#4a6a9881 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=2} 20 two-chain X-ray complexes, each chain over 50 residues, with an exact Kd ([2026-10-30T0000Z_interface-kd_complex-selection](../runs/2026-10-30T0000Z_interface-kd_complex-selection/)). Selection seed `20261030`; no pair exceeded the 70% identity / 70% coverage homology cutoff. Kd spans **1e-15 M to 8e-04 M** — about 12 orders of magnitude, from 1 fM to 790 µM (n = 20). ::: ::: ::: {.caveat} That 12-order span is assembled from different publications using different assay types. A rank correlation across it is measuring agreement between heterogeneous experiments as much as anything structural. Recurating the set is an [open question](../decisions.qmd#pdbbind-recuration). ::: ## Predicted structures: good enough, with four exceptions ::: {#d81897d8 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=3} 20 complexes x 5 models = 100 predictions ([2026-11-03T0000Z_interface-kd_af3-predictions](../runs/2026-11-03T0000Z_interface-kd_af3-predictions/)), ipTM 0.15 to 0.94 over 100 models. Mean DockQ against the crystal structures is **0.688** before relaxation and **0.657** after, over 100 and 100 models ([2026-11-04T0300Z_interface-kd_structure-quality](../runs/2026-11-04T0300Z_interface-kd_structure-quality/)) — a mean change of -0.032. 16 of 20 complexes reach medium or high CAPRI accuracy. ::: ::: ::: {#792afca5 .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

The model knew it was guessing. **5bnq is the problem case.** Mean ipTM 0.85 but DockQ 0.03, with fnat 0 in all five models. Confirmed by an independent alignment-based contact check, so it is not a chain-mapping artefact: it is a confidently wrong prediction. Confidence cannot be used as a filter on its own. ::: ::: ::: {#7ac37de0 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

(That coefficient is transcribed from the report, not recomputed here.) ::: ::: Relaxation slightly degrades agreement with crystal on average and badly in one case: ::: {#774f8ae3 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=8} 4bkx falls from DockQ 0.92 to 0.69 ([2026-11-04T0136Z_interface-kd_fastrelax](../runs/2026-11-04T0136Z_interface-kd_fastrelax/)). FastRelax completed 100/100 models with no failures; 4bkx (658 residues) was rate-limiting at about 50 minutes per model. ::: ::: A further caveat on comparing predictions to crystal at all: ::: {#49a12203 .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=9} **31 of 40 submitted chains contain residues absent from the crystal structures**, up to 113 extra residues in 4bkx ([2026-11-03T0000Z_interface-kd_af3-predictions](../runs/2026-11-03T0000Z_interface-kd_af3-predictions/)). The predictions and the reference structures are not models of identical molecules, which puts a floor under the achievable DockQ for those cases. ::: ::: ## Feature extraction ::: {#7a9e44cf .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=10} All 100 relaxed models went through Rosetta InterfaceAnalyzer, PLIP (inter-chain A–B contacts only), PRODIGY and DockQ, with 200 DockQ comparisons (100 original plus 100 relaxed) and **0 failures** ([2026-11-04T0200Z_interface-kd_interface-metrics](../runs/2026-11-04T0200Z_interface-kd_interface-metrics/)). The sign is negative, so more hydrogen bonds goes with lower log₁₀ Kd, i.e. tighter binding — the direction one would hope for. `dG_norm` is the runner-up and strengthens as wrong models are removed: rho = +0.20 (n = 20, p = 0.39, not significant) to rho = +0.36 (n = 16, p = 0.17, not significant). **Features reaching p < 0.05 by Spearman: 0 of 11 at n = 20, 0 of 11 at n = 16.** None. Across 11 features at these sample sizes, nothing here would survive a correction for multiple comparisons, and the strengthening of `dG_norm` as cases are dropped is equally consistent with real signal recovered from structural error and with noise at n = 16. ::: ::: ### Against the baseline ::: {#1492281c .cell execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=15} | Predictor | Spearman rho vs experimental log₁₀ Kd | n | |---|---|---| | PRODIGY on crystal structures (baseline) | +0.092, not significant | 20 | | PRODIGY on relaxed AF3 models | +0.162, not significant | 20 | | Best interface feature (H-bond count) | -0.383, p = 0.10, not significant | 20 | PRODIGY's own predictions agree between crystal and relaxed models at rho = 0.7 (n = 20) ([2026-11-04T0400Z_interface-kd_correlations](../runs/2026-11-04T0400Z_interface-kd_correlations/)), so swapping crystal structures for relaxed predictions does not much change what PRODIGY says — which supports the predicted-structures-are-usable claim while saying nothing good about accuracy against experiment. ::: ::: ## Where this leaves the track The interface-descriptor hypothesis is **not supported** by this benchmark. The honest summary is that at n = 16–20, with a Kd range spanning 12 orders of magnitude and mixed assay provenance, this experiment cannot distinguish a weak real signal from noise. H-bond count is the only candidate worth carrying forward. Modelling (LASSO / Ridge / ElasticNet) and held-out validation are **not started**, and should not start on these features at this sample size — fitting a regularised model to 11 features and 16–20 points, selected after inspecting correlations, would produce a number with no evidential value. What would change the answer: a larger and better-curated benchmark with consistent assay provenance and a narrower Kd range. That is the [PDBBind recuration question](../decisions.qmd#pdbbind-recuration). Separately, the [AlphaFold Server terms](../decisions.qmd#alphafold-terms) block publication of anything here regardless of the result. ## Runs behind this page ::: {#95a65010 .cell
